quote: An assumption, though false, if persisted in, will harden into fact.
Feeling is the secret. Capture the feeling of the wish fulfilled.
Stop trying to change the world since it is only the mirror. Man's attempt to change the world by force is as fruitless as breaking a mirror in the hope of changing one's face.
Change your conception of yourself and you will automatically change the world in which you live.
You do not attract that which you want, but that which you are.
Sleep is the door through which the conscious, waking mind passes to be creatively joined to the subconscious.
Signs follow, they do not precede.
To reach a higher level of being, you must assume a higher concept of yourself.
Dare to believe in the reality of your assumption and watch the world conform to it.
Assume the feeling of your wish fulfilled and continue therein.
You are already that which you want to be, and your refusal to believe this is the only reason you do not see it.
There is no one to change but self; that self is simply your awareness, your consciousness.
Consciousness is the only reality. It is the first and only cause-substance of the phenomena of life.
The world is yourself pushed out.
Live in the feeling of being the one you want to be, and that you shall be.
Imagination and faith are the secrets of creation.
All transformation begins with an intense, burning desire to be transformed.
Do not waste one moment in regret, for to think feelingly of the mistakes of the past is to reinfect yourself.
Assume the feeling of the wish fulfilled and observe the route that your attention follows.
Be still and know that you are that which you desire to be.
A change of feeling is a change of destiny.
Your opinion of yourself is your most important viewpoint.
The great secret is a controlled imagination and a well-sustained attention firmly and repeatedly focused on the object to be accomplished.
You must assume the feeling of the wish fulfilled until your assumption has all the sensory vividness of reality.
Claim it; enter into the feeling of it, and the world will conform to your assumption.
Man moves in a world that is nothing more or less than his consciousness objectified.
What you sincerely feel yourself to be, you are.
To attempt to change circumstances before you change your imaginal activity is to struggle against the very nature of things.
Deny the evidence of the senses and appropriate the feeling of the wish fulfilled.
Dare to believe that you are what you want to be, and persist in that assumption, for it will harden into fact.
Faith is loyalty to unseen reality.
The undisciplined mind finds it difficult to assume a state which is denied by the senses.
The ideal you seek and strive to attain will not manifest itself until you have imagined that it is already real.
Whatever the mind of man can imagine, man can realize.
Live in the feeling of being the one you want to be.
By desiring, you remain aware of lack; by assuming, you possess.
The cornerstone on which all things are based is man's concept of himself.
Chance or accident is not responsible for the things that happen to you, nor is predestined fate the author of your fortune or misfortune.
To imagine unlovely things is to misuse the creative power within you.
Live in the end, thinking from the end, and not of the end.
Your inner speech is continually outpictured in the world around you.
Everything depends upon your attitude towards yourself. That which you will not affirm as true of yourself can never be realized by you.
Sleep in peace, knowing that the subconscious mind will faithfully objectify your feeling.
To be conscious of being poor while asking for wealth is to be rewarded with that which you are conscious of being — namely, poverty.
Leave the mirror and change your face. Leave the world alone and change your conceptions of yourself.
Whatever you enclose within consciousness becomes your outpictured world.
The subconscious never fails to express that which has been impressed upon it.
The subjective state must be reached before the objective manifestation can appear.
Live as though the wish were already a fact.
Forgiveness is the identification of another with his ideal.
The time it takes your assumption to become fact, your desire to be fulfilled, is directly proportionate to the naturalness of your feeling of already being what you want to be.
Every moment of your life, consciously or unconsciously, you are assuming a feeling. You can no more avoid assuming a feeling than you can avoid eating and drinking.
You must assume the feeling of the fulfillment of your desire until you are possessed by it and this feeling crowds all other ideas out of your consciousness.
The world moves with motiveless necessity. By this is meant that it has no motive of its own, but is under the necessity of manifesting your concept.
Health, wealth, beauty, and genius are not created; they are only manifested by the arrangement of your mind — that is, by your concept of yourself.
Man's chief delusion is his conviction that there are causes other than his own state of consciousness.

When you know that consciousness is the one and only reality, you are free from the tyranny of second causes, free from the belief that there are causes outside of your own mind that can affect your life.
I AM is a feeling of permanent awareness. The very center of consciousness is the feeling of I AM.
You go and prepare a place for yourself by imagining yourself into the feeling of your wish fulfilled.
Since your life is determined by your assumptions, you are forced to recognize the fact that you are either a slave to your assumptions or their master.

Ideas are impressed on the subconscious through the medium of feeling. No idea can be impressed on the subconscious until it is felt, but once felt — be it good, bad or indifferent — it must be expressed.
Feeling is the one and only medium through which ideas are conveyed to the subconscious.
The conscious is the realm of effect; the subconscious is the realm of cause. These two aspects are the male and female divisions of consciousness.
The subconscious is not concerned with the truth or falsity of your feeling. It always accepts as true that which you feel to be true.
To feel 'I will be' is to confess 'I am not'; 'I am' is stronger than 'I am not'. What you feel you are always dominates what you feel you would like to be.
Think feelingly only of the state you desire to realize. Feeling the reality of the state sought and living and acting on that conviction is the way of all seeming miracles.
In defining your objective, you must be concerned only with the objective itself. The manner of expression or the difficulties involved are not to be considered by you.

If you dwell on difficulties, barriers, or delay, the subconscious — by its very non-selective nature — accepts the feeling of difficulties and obstacles as your request and proceeds to produce them in your outer world.
It is easier to ascribe your feeling to events in the world than to admit that the conditions of the world reflect your feeling. However, it is eternally true that the outside mirrors the inside.
When a man believes in the value of the advice given him and applies it, he establishes within himself the reality of success.
Never go to sleep feeling discouraged or dissatisfied. Never sleep in the consciousness of failure.
As the end is accepted, you become totally indifferent as to possible failure, for acceptance of the end wills the means to that end.
Not one thing has ever appeared in man's world but what man decreed that it should.
You do not command things to appear by your words or loud affirmations. Such vain repetition is more often than not a confirmation of the opposite.
The awareness of being is the door through which the manifestations of life pass into the world of form.
To attempt to change the world before you change your concept of yourself is to struggle against the nature of things.
Claim yourself to be that which you want to be and that you will be. Leave all conditions alone.
Do not try to change people; they are only messengers telling you who you are. Revalue yourself and they will confirm the change.
Your world is your consciousness objectified. Waste no time trying to change the outside; change the within or the impression, and the without or expression will take care of itself.
You rise to a higher level of consciousness by taking your attention away from your present limitations and placing it upon that which you desire to be.
To be conscious of being free, healthy, wealthy, or happy is to command these states into being.
Turn your attention away from your problem and the evidence of your senses and assume the feeling of being that which you desire to be.
The man who is not consciously in control of his imagination is at the mercy of every passing mood and circumstance.
All you can possibly need or desire is already yours. You need no helper to give it to you; it is yours now.
When you drop your desire in consciousness as a seed, confident that it shall appear in its full-blown potential, you have done all that is expected of you.
Man is a creature of habit. He surrounds himself with the circumstances of his own habitual state of awareness.
To pray successfully you must have clearly defined objectives. You must know what you want before you can ask for it.
The subjective acceptance of your wish fulfilled produces the objective conditions to correspond with your acceptance.
To be effective, prayer must be felt rather than uttered.
Imagination travels into the future, takes possession of the desired state, and returns to the present to fulfill it.
To become conscious of being that which you desire to be is to pass from the world of shadows into the world of light.
All transformation begins with an uncritical observation of our reactions to life.
Imagination is the real and eternal world of which this vegetable universe is but a faint shadow.
Man is all imagination and God is man and exists in us and we in him. The eternal body of man is the imagination, that is, God himself.
The world of creation is finished and its original is within us. We have only to open our imaginal eyes to perceive it.
The art of revision: this is the greatest of all arts. What you do not like, rewrite.
Stop all negative internal conversations. An internal conversation is an imaginal activity.
Man's mental conversations attract his life. As he talks to himself within, so his world develops without.
Imagining creates reality. What you imagine with feeling will project itself on the screen of space.
You cannot lose what you are conscious of being. You can only lose what you possess by effort.
I firmly believe that if you will wisely and daily use the pruning shears of revision that you will find there is no objective beyond your ability to realize.
Somewhere within this realm of imagination there is a mood, a feeling of the wish fulfilled which, if appropriated, will give the objective reality.
The grain of mustard seed is not the measure of a small amount of faith. On the contrary, it is the absolute in faith.
You have become so enmeshed in the belief that you are man that you have forgotten the glorious being that you are.
The world is a mirror, forever reflecting what you are doing, within yourself.
Man's only natural restriction is his concept of himself.
Every state is a house of many mansions.
A man's state of consciousness is the one and only cause of his world.
To define a state is to personify it; and to personify a state is to become it.
The secret of imagining is the greatest of all problems.
Man's imaginal activity is the one and only cause of his world.
You are that which you contemplate.
The subconscious is the womb of creation.
The feeling of the wish fulfilled is the secret of creation.
Assumptions awaken what they affirm.
Every state has a feeling of its own.
To imagine is to see with the inner eye, and to feel with the inner sense.
The imagination is the creative power of God.
What we did, we imagined and did.
There is an imaginal past and an imaginal future.
Nothing appears or continues in being by a power of its own.
Events happen because comparatively stable imaginal activities created them.
God's will is in you active as your own Imagination.
Your eternal body is the human imagination, and that is God Himself.
A state is an attitude of mind, a body of beliefs.
You can always transcend a state by assuming the feeling of the state you desire to be.
To be in the world, yet not of it, is to remain faithful to the imaginal act.
Every imaginal act influences the outer world.
That which you imagine yourself to be today goes forward and will confront you in the future.
Man is the creator of his own world.
Man's world is his imaginal activity outpictured.
To pray is to control the imagination.
Prayer is the art of believing.
Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
To believe is to accept.
To assume is to take upon oneself.
You must persist in your assumption until it hardens into fact.
The naturalness of your feeling of the wish fulfilled is the secret of all successful prayer.
You are always assuming a feeling, whether you are conscious of it or not.
You must be possessed by the feeling of the wish fulfilled.
To clothe oneself in a state is to become it.
The world is a manifestation of your consciousness.
Your consciousness is the only reality.
Feeling is the secret of creation.
Whatever the mind of man can imagine, man can achieve.
Think from the end.
Revision is repentance. Repentance which I call today revision.
I bring him before my mind's eye and I congratulate him on his good fortune.
To desire a state is to have it.
Matching the beliefs of a state is the seeking that finds, the knocking to which it is opened, the asking that receives.
